findings.title: A member can cancel another member's reservation
findings.author: hunter-authz
findings.impact: Cancels any reservation whose ID the member supplies.
conditions: The attacker has a member account.
The attacker knows or enumerates a reservation ID.

trace.detail: DELETE selects by id only, with no owner filter.

findings.evidence: Invariant: only a reservation's owner may cancel it. The strongest defense, require_member at app/routes.py:19, checks login, not ownership, and the delete at app/reservations.py:42 filters by ID only. Source-only; not reproduced.

reviewer.reason: Reconstructed the path from the route to the query; no middleware adds an owner check.

findings.remediation: Restore owner-only cancellation in the delete itself: add the authenticated member's ID to its condition at app/reservations.py:42, so every route that reaches it is covered.
findings.regression: Unexecuted plan for the fixed revision, with dummy data: member B's cancellation of member A's reservation returns not-found and the reservation remains, a case that fails at 4f2c9e1; A can still cancel A's own reservation.

findings.title: Login may accept unlimited password guesses
findings.author: hunter-auth
findings.impact: Unbounded password guessing against member accounts, if no outside limit applies.
conditions: No proxy or gateway limit caps failed attempts for an account on POST /login.

trace.detail: Each request checks the password without counting failures.

findings.evidence: The application has no limit; the deployment limit is unknown.

reviewer.reason: The application code is as described; the outcome depends on the proxy.

findings.blocker: The proxy configuration for POST /login is not in the repository.
findings.next_check: Ask the operator for the effective proxy limits on POST /login: a cap on failed attempts per account refutes the claim; no such cap confirms it.

findings.title: Sort column interpolated into SQL
findings.author: hunter-injection

trace.detail: sort comes from the query string.
The column name is formatted into the query.

findings.evidence: app/search.py:9 maps sort through a fixed dictionary and rejects other values; the only query using the result is at line 12.

reviewer.reason: Only allowlisted column names reach the query.

findings.reason: The allowlist at app/search.py:9 admits only fixed column names, and the only query that uses sort, at line 12, runs after it, so no path passes raw input into SQL.

scanners.preflight: Plain pip-audit -r can install packages. This candidate needs fully pinned requirements and installed-version proof of no package execution or unredacted output; network use is also unapproved.

gitleaks is not installed. A run also needs --config naming trusted rules outside the target; otherwise the target's .gitleaks.toml may replace or allowlist detection rules. Verify installed-version redaction, network behavior and target-controlled exclusions before running.
